title: Publishing

## Rendering in CI

When rendering as part of an automated pipeline, pass `--strict` to
treat warnings as errors:

```bash
quarto render --strict
```

Under `--strict`, any diagnostic that would normally be reported as a
warning — an unresolved cross-reference, an undefined template
variable, a warning raised by a Lua filter — is reported as an error
instead, and the command exits with a non-zero status. The render
itself still runs to completion, so a single invocation reports every
problem in the project rather than stopping at the first one.

A render that produces no warnings behaves identically with and
without the flag.

## Suppressing diagnostics

Sometimes Quarto warns about something your project does on purpose.
The `diagnostics:` key turns a specific warning off, by error code:

```yaml
# _quarto.yml
diagnostics:
  Q-2-49: off
```

Every warning Quarto prints carries its code in brackets — `[Q-2-49]` —
and each code has a documentation page explaining what it means. Read
that page before silencing it: most warnings are worth fixing rather
than hiding.

When you do silence one, say why. The long form takes a reason:

```yaml
diagnostics:
  Q-2-49:
    level: off
    reason: "bare spans are markers for our annotate.lua filter"
```

The reason is optional, but it is what lets the next person to read the
file decide whether the suppression still applies. A bare code list
records *that* you dissented; a reason records *why*.

`diagnostics:` works in `_quarto.yml` for a whole project, in a
directory's `_metadata.yml`, or in a single document's front matter,
following the same precedence as any other Quarto setting — a document
overrides its directory, which overrides the project. It applies to
`quarto render` and `quarto preview` alike, so a construct you have
declared legitimate does not reappear as a warning while you are
editing.

Two things `diagnostics:` deliberately cannot do:

- **It cannot suppress errors**, only warnings and informational
  messages. Silencing an error would mean publishing broken output with
  no indication that anything went wrong.
- **It cannot suppress a diagnostic that has no code.** A few of
  Quarto's warnings do not carry one yet.

Suppression is applied before `--strict` promotes warnings to errors,
so a suppressed warning stays suppressed in CI rather than reappearing
as a build failure.
